topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, target audience, and primary learning objectives for cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular, genetic, and tissue-level basis of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental nature of cancer as an accumulation of genetic alterations and a failure of tissue differentiation, alongside laboratory models used to study it.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors progress from contained benign states to locally invasive and metastatic malignancies, illustrated through clinical and histological examples.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature conventions and exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard rules and exceptions used to name benign and malignant neoplasms according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer-related morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and structural ways that primary and metastatic tumors impair organ function to cause illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiology and comparative incidence of tumors across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore cancer frequency and mortality patterns in human populations and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address clinical tumor detection, exploring the rationale, histological foundations, and limitations of population screening programmes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session by referencing the learning outcomes and providing logistical instructions for upcoming practicals.
